identification: Blue and white vitreous enamel advertising sign 'LEADING NEWSPAPER. THE DAILY TELEGRAPH. TASMANIA.', MADE IN ENGLAND lower right. Launceston Daily Telegraph (1883-1928) so pre-1928. Genuine enamel on iron. Large loss and rust top right with jagged edge, edge and fixing-hole chips, reverse heavily rusted, face bright. About 3:1 landscape format.

entries.note: ENAMEL STREET SIGN - QUEENS AVENUE, 8 bids, hammer, premium extra. Local street sign, not advertising; API result opened. Shows local named enamel signs can pass $100.
Vintage enamel car rally/Targa sign 91.5 x 36.5cm, 9 bids, hammer. Probably a modern repro-style item; weak guide.
Enamel Esso sign, 3 bids, hammer. Condition unknown; likely a later or reproduction piece.
RARE SHELL MOTOR OIL ENAMEL SIGN, hammer, 0 bids listed (likely a data quirk). Petrol signs are a far stronger collecting category than newspaper signs; upper-bound only, not comparable.

viewing_check: Measure the sign, confirm it is true vitreous enamel (not tin), check for any maker mark on the reverse or edge, and photograph the top-right loss close up to see how much face lettering is affected and whether the rest is stable.
